Use gpt-6.1-sol xhigh. Offline CODE task. Root exclusively owns all UART/USB/hardware/Windows/network/credentials and is currently running a board test. Do not touch them. Own ONLY a new backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-page-budget32/ directory. Do not modify maintained trees, frozen outputs or the read-service adapter. No downloads/upgrades. Preserve dirty sources.
Latest user direction: if openvela faster than original/default ESP-IDF, reduce proven negative resource/safety/stability tradeoffs while retaining IDF-level rates; slower cases continue optimization. Astra analysis complete: read backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-default-reference-followup/cost-audit.md, especially FS pool audit/F contract. Prepare ONE small reversible resource candidate: derive from frozen FS06 B at openvela-dev/out/esp32s31-korvo-stdioseek-b-20261023, change only global COALESCE_MAX_PAGES64→32 in actual page pool implementation. Keep per-mount updates64, all correctness/COW/fsync/close/shared-handle semantics, geometry, FILE64, staging, flags and actual numbered apps. Do not add diagnostic instrumentation or WEL patch, those are separate. The change reduces dynamic PSRAM page cap256→128KiB, not guaranteed actual allocation savings. Static pointer table expected256→128B; verify actual RV32 symbol/ELF rather than claim blindly.
Use existing isolated build machinery and local locked dependencies, preferably existing korvo-fs-read-service build preparation pattern WITHOUT its instrumentation. Read relevant README/AGENTS. Rebase source links and preserve exact baseline compile flags/config. Build paired kernel+AppFS, verify unchanged app outputs/config, review exact source delta and receipts; no hardware runner needed now. Do not copy stale B object files as proof of new build. Capture build and exact artifacts/source hashes. Candidate and frozen B must remain independently identifiable.
Reuse meaningful existing littlefs-random-write-coalescing/vfs-v1 NOR/VFS host fixture(s) to compare original64 vscandidate32 at affected boundaries: page33 triggers early sync, shared handles/two files, pool exhaustion on another mount, allocation/fault propagation and clean page returns. If existing test assumes64, adapt only isolated fixtures with stated expected contracts; do not weaken errors or mislabel hardware proof. No need broad new framework/test boilerplate or full upstream suite. Run required focused tests and appropriate build; stop repeating after they pass. Deliver concise README, candidate.patch, frozen pair/config/source receipt, actual resource delta and material uncertainties (early COW/erase amplification and tail latency await board). No xTS acceptance or performance claims. Finish with concrete ready handoff; Root will decide board comparison after ongoing network/service diagnostics.

I’ll inspect the FS audit and isolated build pattern, then build and host-test the 32-page candidate inside the new directory. I’ll leave hardware, network, maintained sources, and frozen outputs untouched.

The audit confirms that the global page pool and per-mount `updates[64]` are separate. I’ll retain `updates[64]` and use FS06 B directly, excluding the read-service instrumentation and WEL patch. The host comparison will check both the earlier flush at page 33 and allocation failure when another mount owns the pool.

The isolated preparation is checking frozen B’s artifacts and ABI receipt before copying its sources. I’ll preserve its compiler options, config, and build metadata so any object difference can be traced to the one-line page-cap change.

The clean kernel/AppFS build passed with B’s config unchanged, and the original 64-page host fixture passed. I’ll now run the 32-page fixture and audit the build outputs, including the actual RV32 `g_pages` symbol and all application hashes.

Both host variants passed the focused checks, including page 33, shared handles, two files, cross-mount exhaustion, allocation and I/O failures, and page returns.

The RV32 ELF confirms `g_pages` shrinks from 256 to 128 bytes; total BSS drops by 128 bytes, with text and data unchanged. The 33-page NOR model also shows extra commits and erases with the smaller pool. I’ll include that cost in the handoff; board latency and allocation savings remain unmeasured.

Ready for Root’s review: [README and handoff](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-page-budget32/README.md).

- Only global `COALESCE_MAX_PAGES` changes 64→32; `updates[64]` remains.
- Clean kernel/AppFS build and both focused ASan/UBSan host runs passed.
- Config, all 21 app ELFs and AppFS match frozen B.
- RV32 confirms **128 B less BSS**. Dynamic PSRAM capacity falls **128 KiB**; actual savings remain unmeasured.
- The page33 model increases erases **72→112**. Board rates and tail latency await Root’s comparison.

Separate frozen/candidate pairs, hashes, patch and receipts are included. Protected sources remain unchanged; hardware was untouched.
